audit_findings.title: Growth may depend on acquisition spending omitted from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed: $202.403 million fiscal-2026 acquisition outlays and 3.6 percentage points of sales growth versus 2.0 points organic; computed: growth assumptions create a $26.75 per-share bear-to-bull valuation spread
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquisition-funded growth enters the forecast growth rate while acquisition cash outlays are excluded from distributable owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: As an important part of our growth strategy, we intend to continue pursuing acquisitions of complementary businesses or products and creating joint ventures.
audit_findings.explanation: This is not yet a demonstrated calculation error because the record does not establish how much acquisition spending is required prospectively. It is nevertheless reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion: acquisitions supplied more fiscal-2026 growth than the organic business, the annual acquisition outlay equaled 32.4% of the $624.6 million OE anchor, and growth is a major valuation driver.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild historical OE and sales growth on a constant organic perimeter, estimate recurring acquisition investment needed for each growth scenario, and rerun the DCF using organic growth or OE net of that investment.

audit_findings.title: Known litigation claim is accrued only at the bottom of a large range
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed: up to $152.0 million above the $0.5 million accrual, plus unquantified postjudgment interest; computed: $1.16 per share before additional interest
audit_findings.mechanism: Any loss above the accrual is a claim ahead of equity and would require a direct bridge deduction or reduce future OE when paid.
audit_findings.evidence: We currently estimate a range of possible outcomes between approximately $ 0.5 million and $ 152.5 million, which is inclusive of the prejudgment interest awarded (but exclusive of any accruing postjudgment interest), and we accrued a liability as of August 31, 2024, at the low end of the range, as no amount within the range is a better estimate than any other amount.
audit_findings.explanation: The unresolved appellate exposure is real but is not a demonstrated valuation error. Even deducting the full filed amount above the accrual would reduce base value from $74.48 to approximately $73.32 per share and bull value from $87.17 to approximately $86.01, both still below the $105.52 market price. Accruing postjudgment interest is unquantified but would have to be very large relative to the filed range to reverse that conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the latest appellate docket, applicable postjudgment interest calculation, insurance recovery evidence and recorded accrual; rerun the bridge if net exposure exceeds the accrual.

audit_findings.title: Marketable equities added as stakes may back insurance claims
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed: $174.394 million; computed: $1.33 per share and 1.8% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds securities to equity value even though claim-backing assets or required captive capital may not be distributable surplus.
audit_findings.evidence: We carry a portion of our marketable securities portfolio in long-term assets since they are generally held for the settlement of our general and product liability insurance claims processed through our wholly owned captive insurance subsidiaries.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that a portion of the portfolio supports captive-insurance claims, but it does not identify the restricted portion, so an overstatement is possible rather than proven. Even removing the entire $174.4 million bridge addition would reduce base value to approximately $73.15 and bull value to approximately $85.84 per share, leaving the valuation conclusion unchanged.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the captive portfolios to loss reserves, incurred-but-not-reported claims and regulatory capital, then replace stakes_net with only unrestricted surplus.

audit_findings.title: Nearly all bridge cash is held in foreign subsidiaries
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed: $291.8 million foreign cash; computed: $2.23 per share and 3.0% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash added in the equity bridge may require operating retention or incur repatriation leakage, reducing the amount distributable to shareholders.
audit_findings.evidence: As of May 31, 2026, approximately $291.8 million of our consolidated cash and cash equivalents were held at various foreign subsidiaries, compared with approximately $274.9 million as of May 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: Foreign location is demonstrated, but non-transferability and repatriation leakage are not. Even excluding all $291.8 million of foreign cash would reduce base value to approximately $72.25 and bull value to approximately $84.94 per share, still below the $105.52 market price; therefore this finding cannot change the present valuation conclusion on the supplied scale.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a jurisdiction-level cash schedule showing legal availability, permanent-reinvestment designation, minimum operating cash and withholding or repatriation taxes, then rerun the bridge with net transferable excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Anchor earnings contain a noncash earnout remeasurement gain
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed: $14.418 million pretax gain and $5.349 million remaining contingent-consideration liability; computed: gain equals 2.3% of anchor OE and approximately $1.63 per share of base value if fully capitalized
audit_findings.mechanism: If not purged, the nonrecurring gain inflates anchor OE and every forecast year; any unpaid earnout is separately a claim in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: This was partially offset by a $14.4 million gain on earn-out liability fair value adjustments primarily associated with the Star Brands Group acquisition, along with MAP 2025 benefits, savings from 2026 restructuring actions and decreased professional fees related to our MAP 2025 initiatives.
audit_findings.explanation: The gain is demonstrated, but its inclusion in OE is not: the filed cash-flow statement explicitly reverses the $14.418 million noncash gain when reconciling operating cash flow. Even if the full pretax gain remained in the anchor, scaling it by the supplied base operating-PV-to-OE ratio gives approximately $213.8 million, or $1.63 per share; the remaining liability adds only about $0.04 per share. That scale does not change the conclusion that value is below the market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $624.6 million OE calculation line by line to the cash-flow statement, confirm the gain reversal, and verify whether the $5.349 million contingent-consideration liability is already captured before deciding on a bridge deduction.

audit_findings.title: Environmental obligations exist for sites with no recorded accrual
audit_findings.mechanism: Existing remediation obligations above recorded reserves would reduce equity through future cash payments or a direct bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: As a result, accruals have not been estimated for certain of these sites and costs may ultimately exceed existing estimated accruals for other sites.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that some existing sites have no estimated accrual and that other site costs may exceed reserves, so this is more than a purely forward-looking risk. However, the record provides no site-level cost range, probability, timing, insurance recovery or collectible indemnity amount; materiality therefore cannot be established. Recorded environmental reserves total $8.858 million, but they do not cap the disclosed exposure.
audit_findings.action: Obtain site-level remediation ranges, allocation percentages, payment timing, insurance coverage and indemnitor credit evidence; calculate exposure above the $8.858 million recorded reserve and rerun the equity bridge if estimable.
